subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The baker was meticulous. She measured every cup of flour with great care." What does "meticulous" mean?

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The soap bubble was ephemeral. It popped a moment after it formed." What does "ephemeral" mean?
hint: Think about how fast the bubble popped.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Phones are ubiquitous. You can see them in every room, shop, and park." What does "ubiquitous" mean?
hint: The clue is every room, shop, and park.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Mia gave a candid answer. She told her friend exactly what she thought." What does "candid" mean?
hint: She told what she really thought.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Leo is frugal. He saves his coins and spends them only on things he needs." What does "frugal" mean?
hint: Think about how he treats his coins.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Sam was reluctant to jump in the cold pool. He stood at the edge for a long time." What does "reluctant" mean?
hint: He stood at the edge and waited.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Typewriters are mostly obsolete. Most people now use computers." What does "obsolete" mean?
hint: Most people use something else now.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Ana is gregarious. She loves parties and talks to everyone she meets." What does "gregarious" mean?
hint: She loves to be with people.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The tenacious puppy kept pulling the rope. It would not let go." What does "tenacious" mean?
hint: The puppy would not let go.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The speech was verbose. It used a hundred words where ten would do." What does "verbose" mean?
hint: Compare a hundred words to ten.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The coach was lenient. When players came late, she only said, "Be on time next game."" What does "lenient" mean?
hint: She did not give a big punishment.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Dev took a pragmatic view. He picked the plan that would really work, not the fanciest one." What does "pragmatic" mean?
hint: He cared about what really works.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The mouse found a meager meal. It was just two crumbs." What does "meager" mean?
hint: Two crumbs is not much.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The benevolent king gave warm coats to every child in the town." What does "benevolent" mean?
hint: Think about why he gave coats.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Washing the same dishes each day felt mundane to Rosa." What does "mundane" mean?
hint: Doing the same task each day feels this way.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The inventor leaned in to scrutinize the tiny gear." What does "scrutinize" mean?
hint: She leaned in to look.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Bees visit flowers to drink sweet nectar. As they travel, pollen sticks to their legs. They carry it to the next flower, and this helps plants make seeds.
hint: Ask what the bees do for the plants.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Sleep gives the body time to rest. During sleep, the brain sorts what you learned that day. People who sleep well often think more clearly.
choices: Good sleep helps the body and mind.
Sleep takes up a lot of time.
answer: Good sleep helps the body and mind.
hint: Look for the idea that all three sentences share.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: A library lends books for free. Many also offer computers, quiet rooms, and story hours. A library card is all you need to start.
hint: What do all the sentences say about the library?

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Trees in a city give cool shade on hot days. Their leaves clean the air. Birds also build nests in them.
choices: City trees help people and animals.
answer: City trees help people and animals.
hint: Think about who gains from the trees.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Food scraps can become rich soil. Worms and tiny living things break the scraps down. Gardeners then spread this soil on their plants.
choices: Food scraps can be turned into soil for gardens.
answer: Food scraps can be turned into soil for gardens.
hint: Follow what happens to the scraps.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: At first, Nia could not ride her bike without falling. She practiced each day for a week. Soon she rode all the way to the park.
hint: What changed from the start to the end?

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: The moon pulls on the ocean. This pull makes the water rise and fall twice a day. We call these changes tides.
choices: The moon is bright at night.
hint: What makes the water rise and fall?

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: One ant cannot carry a big crumb. But many ants can lift it together. They work as a team to bring food home.
choices: Ants work together to move food.
answer: Ants work together to move food.
hint: Look at what the ants do as a team.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Long ago, sailors used stars to find their way at sea. One star in the north always stays in the same spot. It showed them which way to go.
choices: Sailors used stars to find their way.
answer: Sailors used stars to find their way.
hint: What did the sailors use the stars for?

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Old paper can be turned into new paper. First it is mixed with water to make a soft pulp. Then the pulp is pressed flat and dried.
choices: Old paper can be made into new paper.
answer: Old paper can be made into new paper.
hint: Think about the steps from old to new.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: A cactus lives where rain is rare. Its thick stem stores water for dry days. Its spines give shade and keep animals away.
choices: A cactus has ways to live in dry places.
answer: A cactus has ways to live in dry places.
hint: Each sentence tells how it handles dry land.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: When Omar saw a new student eating alone, he sat down beside her. They talked about games and laughed. By the end of lunch, she had a new friend.
choices: Lunch is the best part of school.
Games are more fun than books.
A small act of kindness can make a friend.
answer: A small act of kindness can make a friend.
hint: What did Omar do, and what came of it?

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: One of the boys ___ ready.
hint: The subject is one. It is a single person.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence uses the right they-re word?

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: The dog wagged ___ tail.
hint: You need the word that shows the tail belongs to the dog.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: Mom gave the map to Jo and ___.
hint: Try it without Jo. Mom gave the map to ___.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: Each of the cats ___ a bell.
hint: Each means one at a time.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence uses commas the right way?
choices: We packed apples pears, and grapes.
We packed apples, pears, and grapes.
We packed, apples pears and grapes.
We, packed apples, pears and grapes.
answer: We packed apples, pears, and grapes.
hint: Commas go between the things in a list.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: I would have gone if I ___ known.
hint: The sentence talks about the past.

subject: reading
prompt: Which word is the verb in this sentence? The tall robot waved quickly.
hint: Find the action word.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: We have ___ apples than we did.
hint: You can count apples one by one.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence asks who owns the coat?
hint: You want the word that asks who owns it.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence compares the right way?
choices: She speaks more clearer than her brother.
She speaks most clearly than her brother.
She speaks more clearly than her brother.
She speaks clearlier than her brother.
answer: She speaks more clearly than her brother.
hint: Pick the one with a single comparing word.

subject: reading
prompt: Which one is a full sentence, not a piece of one?
hint: A full sentence tells who did what.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "exuberant" mean? "The exuberant puppy raced around the yard, wagging its whole body."
hint: Look at how the puppy moves.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "tentative" mean? "Their plans for the trip were tentative, so nothing was booked yet."
hint: Nothing was booked.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "substantiate" mean? "She brought photos to substantiate her story."
hint: Why would someone bring photos along?

subject: reading
prompt: What does "diminish" mean? "The storm began to diminish, and soon the sky was clear."
hint: The sky became clear afterward.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "versatile" mean? "A versatile jacket can be worn in rain, wind, or sun."
hint: Rain, wind, and sun are all covered.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "contemplate" mean? "He sat by the lake to contemplate his next move in the chess game."
hint: He sat quietly to do it.

subject: reading
prompt: What does "inhabit" mean? "Many kinds of birds inhabit the wetlands near our town."
hint: Think about where the birds make their home.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this passage?
passage: Before clocks were common, towns used bells to mark the hours. The sound traveled across fields and rooftops, so workers far from town knew when to stop for lunch. Today, we check phones instead of listening for bells.
choices: Bells once helped people keep track of time.
answer: Bells once helped people keep track of time.
hint: Ask what the bells were used for.

subject: reading
prompt: Why is staying calm important for a diver?
passage: Pearl divers hold their breath for a minute or more. They train their lungs for years, and they learn to stay calm underwater. Staying calm saves oxygen.
hint: Read the last short sentence.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the planner's goal?
passage: A city planner studies how people move through a town. She decides where to put parks, bike lanes, and bus stops. Her goal is to make the town easy and pleasant for everyone to use.
choices: To make the town easy and pleasant to use.
To count the people in town.
answer: To make the town easy and pleasant to use.
hint: Find the sentence that begins with "Her goal."

subject: reading
prompt: Which lesson fits this story best?
passage: Mina missed the last word in the spelling bee by one letter. She felt upset at first. Then she read the word again, wrote it ten times, and cheered for the winner. The next year, she tried again.
hint: Notice what Mina did the next year.

subject: reading
prompt: How do toads move?
passage: Frogs and toads look alike, but they have differences. Frogs have smooth, moist skin and long legs for leaping. Toads have dry, bumpy skin and shorter legs, so they hop or walk.
hint: Look at their legs.

subject: reading
prompt: What is one limit of wind turbines?
passage: Wind turbines turn the power of moving air into electricity. They make no smoke, and the wind is free. Still, they work only when the wind blows, so many places use other sources too.
choices: They work only when the wind blows.
They make a lot of smoke.
answer: They work only when the wind blows.
hint: Look for the word "Still."

subject: reading
prompt: Why did many people gather around televisions?
passage: Many years ago, people watched astronauts walk on the moon. Millions gathered around televisions to see the pictures. Many say it was a moment that made the world feel small and close.
choices: To see astronauts walk on the moon.
answer: To see astronauts walk on the moon.
hint: Read the first sentence.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: The group of students ___ leaving now.
hint: Treat the group as one single thing.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence uses "who" or "whom" correctly?
choices: To who did you give the note?
Who did you give the note to whom?
To whom did you give the note?
answer: To whom did you give the note?
hint: Try "to him" and "to he." Which sounds right?

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: The cat jumped ___ the fence and landed in the garden.

prompt: Which sentence keeps the list parallel?

She likes swimming, to hike, and reading.
answer: She likes swimming, hiking, and reading.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?

Pack these: items a tent, a map, and a lamp.
Pack: these items a tent, a map, and a lamp.
answer: Pack these items: a tent, a map, and a lamp.

prompt: Which word means almost the same as "begin"?

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Her story was plausible, so the teacher believed it." What does "plausible" mean?
hint: The teacher believed it.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "A judge must be impartial and treat both sides fairly." What does "impartial" mean?
hint: Look at the words treat both sides fairly.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Ana felt ambivalent about moving. She was excited to see a new city, but sad to leave her friends." What does "ambivalent" mean?
hint: She felt excited and sad at the same time.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The bright red kite was conspicuous against the gray sky." What does "conspicuous" mean?
hint: Bright red stands out against gray.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The goal in the last minute was pivotal to the win." What does "pivotal" mean?
hint: One goal decided the game.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The crowd broke into spontaneous cheers." What does "spontaneous" mean?
hint: No one told the crowd to cheer.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "The eloquent speaker moved the audience with her words." What does "eloquent" mean?
hint: Her words moved the audience.

subject: reading
prompt: Read: "Her lucid explanation made the hard idea easy to follow." What does "lucid" mean?
hint: The hard idea became easy.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Coral reefs cover only a small part of the ocean floor. Yet they shelter a huge share of sea life. Fish find food and safe hiding places among the coral.
choices: Coral reefs cover most of the ocean.
Coral is a kind of food.
Coral reefs are small but support a lot of sea life.
answer: Coral reefs are small but support a lot of sea life.
hint: Notice the word yet. It joins two ideas.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Early explorers had to guess how far they had traveled. Then clocks became accurate enough to work at sea. With the right time, sailors could find their position far better.
choices: Accurate clocks helped sailors find where they were.
answer: Accurate clocks helped sailors find where they were.
hint: Ask what the clocks made possible.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Marcus had always disliked reading aloud. When his class started a reading club for younger kids, he agreed to help. After seeing a child laugh at his funny voices, he began to look forward to every session.
choices: Helping others changed how Marcus felt about reading aloud.
answer: Helping others changed how Marcus felt about reading aloud.
hint: Compare how Marcus felt at the start and at the end.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Many cities are adding rooftop gardens. The plants keep buildings cooler, soak up rain, and give people a place to rest. Some even grow vegetables for local shops.
choices: Rooftop gardens offer many benefits to cities.
Buildings are too hot in winter.
answer: Rooftop gardens offer many benefits to cities.
hint: The passage lists several good things the gardens do.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Languages change over time. New words appear, old ones fade, and sounds shift from one generation to the next. A book from long ago can seem hard to read for this reason.
choices: New words are better than old ones.
hint: Every sentence gives an example of change.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of this story?
passage: Honest feedback can feel uncomfortable. Still, it shows us what to fix. Athletes, writers, and builders all improve faster when someone points out what is not working.
choices: Feedback should always be kept secret.
Honest feedback, though hard to hear, helps people improve.
answer: Honest feedback, though hard to hear, helps people improve.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: The results of the survey ___ surprising.
hint: The subject is results, which is plural.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: She plays the violin ___ than anyone in the band.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence uses affect and effect correctly?
choices: The weather will effect our plans, and the affect may be a delay.
The weather will affect our plans, and the affect may be a delay.
The weather will effect our plans, and the effect may be a delay.
The weather will affect our plans, and the effect may be a delay.
answer: The weather will affect our plans, and the effect may be a delay.

subject: reading
prompt: Pick the word that fits: If I ___ you, I would ask for help.

subject: reading
prompt: Which sentence is parallel in form?
choices: She likes hiking, to swim, and biking.
She likes hiking, swimming, and biking.
She likes to hike, swimming, and to bike.
She likes hiking, swim, and biking.
answer: She likes hiking, swimming, and biking.

prompt: Pick the word that fits: The prize will go to ___ finishes first.
